newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends firm on concern over crop problems.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends firm on concern over crop problems.

text.p: KCBT wheat futures settled mostly higher on concern about the potentially damaging effects of leaf rust fungus and dry weather in areas of the hard red winter wheat belt, traders said.

"We saw retail speculative buying in here today because of the attention being given to dryness along the western end of the HRW wheat belt. But the market is also antsy over further yield losses in Oklahoma because of leaf rust," a trader said.
Meteorologists told Reuters Friday that dry hard red winter wheat areas of western Kansas probably will not receive the showers that were originally expected for the area.
"We are expecting 90 degree (F) temperatures and strong winds across the drought areas (over the weekend)," one trader said at the midsession.
KCBT wheat also drew support from continued tight cash wheat supplies. Basis bids at some locations in eastern Kansas were reported to have risen Friday by another 10 cents per bushel.
KCBT wheat settled six cents per bushel lower to five cents higher, with May up two cents at $4.70. New crop July was up five cents at $4.24.
Traders said Refco and FIMAT each bought approximately 1.5 million July bushels. Benson-Quinn and Chicago Corp each bought one million July.
